pending_commit.commit_message: cryptohome: pre-fetch and post-assign struct fields For OpenSSL 1.1+, RSA (and other) structures become opaque, meaning it is no longer possible to directly access their fields. Instead get and set accessors are provided by the 1.1 API. Prepare for the OpenSSL-1.1 conversion by implementing some pre-fetching and post-assigning now. This will make this part of the conversion patch simpler to review since it will just replace these direct accesses with the accessors. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:738857 TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-sarien cryptohome => Passes all unittests Change-Id: Ifca4752a25b033d1aee1fc4ea1788a12a7ad1888 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1764848 Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org>

attestation: Use RSA_generate_key_ex() As of OpenSSL 0.9.8, RSA_generate_key() is deprecated in favor of RSA_generate_key_ex(). RSA_generate_key_ex() requires passing in a BIGNUM* exponent, for which we use a crypto::ScopedBIGNUM. The end result is no functional change, but better alignment for openssl 1.1 migration and/or boringssl. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:738816 TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-sarien attestation Change-Id: Ifcd28069ed631d6ddb40919cb0960d4d29330828 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1764849 Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org>

trunks: pre-fetch and post-assign struct fields For OpenSSL 1.1+, RSA (and other) structures become opaque, meaning it is no longer possible to directly access their fields. Instead get and set accessors are provided by the 1.1 API. Prepare for the OpenSSL-1.1 conversion by implementing some pre-fetching and post-assigning now. This will make this part of the conversion patch simpler to review since it will just replace these direct accesses with the accessors. We also add a bit more object allocation/creation failure detection. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:737913 TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-sarien trunks Change-Id: Iab6143d4d53cfc8f2e9405c2463c184b51fff48e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1764854 Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org>

chaps: Update for OpenSSL 1.1 OpenSSL 1.1 has made significant non-backwards compatible changes to its API as outlined in: https://wiki.openssl.org/index.php/OpenSSL_1.1.0_Changes Among other things that have changed are new()/free() semantics for the various CTX structs, which are also conveniently wrapped in libchrome Scoped* objects. This allows us to simplify and better manage the context lifecycles. Note: there is one small behavior change buried in this CL. RSA_set0_key() requires that both n & e be non-null. Thus, in session_impl.c::CreateRSAKeyFromObject, when creating a private RSA key, we must now also always parse out the PUBLIC exponent such that it can be set along with the modulus and private exponent. BUG=chromium:738288 TEST=cros_workon --board=betty start chaps TEST=w/ openssl-1.0.2r: FEATURES=test emerge-betty chaps TEST=w/ openssl-1.1.0j: FEATURES=test emerge-betty chaps => Both build ok and pass all unittests Cq-Depend: chromium:555191, chromium:1699447 Change-Id: I3d804c0ae94468c3390b9bdc010be5ac4234281d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/557562 Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org>

chromeos-config: match ARM architecture more broadly veyron_mighty uses the architecture string "armv7l", which we did not account for in our list of machine types. More broadly match arm machine types by looking for "arm" or "aarch64" as the beginning of the string. The reason this matters is veyron_mighty, despite being non-unibuild, needs to fallback to mosys, and architecture detection needs to happen before mosys can be run. BUG=chromium:991653,chromium:1009475 TEST=sudo FEATURES=test emerge chromeos-config-tools TEST=cros_config /firmware image-name now runs "mosys platform model" on veyron_mighty instead of failing Change-Id: Iefa7f335f117b89894d6215bd0de75bd49a8d767 Signed-off-by: Jack Rosenthal <jrosenth@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1849427 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Abe Levkoy <alevkoy@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Simon Glass <sjg@chromium.org>

arc-setup: change initialization of CrosConfig With CL:1809879, CrosConfig::InitModel() will no longer return false on non-unibuild platforms, as fallback support to mosys was added to libcros_config. Therefore, if CrosConfig::Init fails, there really is something wrong; fail loudly. In addition, InitModel is now just a deprecated alias to Init. Change to Init while we are here.
